channel.title: The U-Curve Brain
channel.description: A macro-autonomous cognitive filter. Optimizing for agency, perspective, and resilience.

item.title: (Video) Animal Perception of Human Music
item.description:
Source: Howtown



This video explores current research into how various animal species perceive and react to human-made music. It investigates whether animals demonstrate preferences, emotional responses, or physiological changes when exposed to different musical compositions and sounds.

item.title: (Video) Bradley Hillier-Smith: Ethics of State Responses to Refugees
item.description:
Source: The Dissenter



Bradley Hillier-Smith discusses the ethical dimensions of various state responses to refugee movements and asylum seekers. The presentation examines moral obligations, international law, and practical challenges governments face when formulating policies related to refugee protection and integration.

item.title: (Video) Acquired Metabolism and Evolutionary Innovation
item.description:
Source: Santa Fe Institute



This presentation by Holly Moeller explores acquired metabolism, a biological phenomenon where organisms obtain metabolic capabilities from other species. It discusses how such horizontal gene transfer and symbiotic relationships can significantly drive evolutionary innovation and adaptation.

item.title: (Research) Sanctuary Cities: Impact and Effectiveness
item.description:
Source: Reasons to be Cheerful

This article examines the concept and operational impact of sanctuary cities, which limit cooperation with federal immigration enforcement. It explores how these policies affect immigrant communities and local governance, often through historical and contemporary case studies.

item.title: (Video) Fluid Dynamics in Closed Conduit Hydraulics
item.description:
Source: Practical Engineering



This video explores the principles of closed conduit hydraulics, a field where fluid dynamics often challenge common intuition. It demonstrates specific examples where expected outcomes diverge from actual physical behavior in constrained liquid systems.

item.title: (Research) Prison Program Conserves Endangered Butterflies in Washington State
item.description:
Source: Reasons to be Cheerful

A conservation program within a women’s prison in Washington state is successfully breeding endangered butterflies. Inmates manage greenhouses, nurturing host plants and larvae to support the recovery of these vulnerable species. This initiative highlights innovative approaches to conservation.

item.title: (Video) Scientific Theories on the Moon's Origin
item.description:
Source: Howtown



This video explores the leading scientific theories and hypotheses regarding the formation and origin of Earth's Moon. It examines evidence and models that explain how the Moon may have come into existence and its early history.

item.title: (Video) Art and Performance Deepen Understanding of Disability
item.description:
Source: The British Academy



This video explores how art, performance, and creative expression can deepen societal understanding of disability. It examines how these mediums offer powerful ways to share and convey the lived experiences of individuals with disabilities.

item.title: (Video) Icelandic Scientists Control Lava Flows
item.description:
Source: TED-Ed



Scientists in Iceland employ three distinct strategies to manage and control lava flows from volcanic eruptions. These methods aim to mitigate risks and protect local communities and infrastructure from the destructive force of future lava advancements.

item.title: (Video) Africa's Turkana Rift Shows Continental Splitting
item.description:
Source: Dr Ben Miles



The Earth's crust beneath Africa's Turkana Rift is thinning to 13 km. This geological process represents the first direct observation of 'necking' in an active continental rift zone, indicating ongoing continental separation.

System Note: Continental drift is a continuous geological process occurring over millions of years, not an immediate or short-term event.

item.title: (Research) Global Childhood Stunting Rates Declined in 20th Century
item.description:
Source: Our World in Data

Global childhood stunting rates decreased significantly throughout the 20th century. Japan's success in reducing its stunting rate from 70% to 5%, offers a historical case study for contemporary public health efforts in affected regions.

item.title: (Adage) Faith will move mountains (Trust your capacity to overcome challenges, reducing fear.)
Today's Pattern: Humanity's relentless pursuit to decipher and direct existence
item.description:
(Today) From geological shifts to human ingenuity, the world is in constant motion. Embrace the power of understanding and action to navigate its complexities.

(Pattern) Across scales, humanity constantly analyzes grand natural processes and proactively applies knowledge to shape outcomes and improve conditions.

(Reminder) Your mind reacts the same to a looming possibility as an immediate problem; master your calm by acting only on what's truly within your present control.
